evals.prompt: I'm setting up Mapbox Maps SDK in my iOS app. Where do I put the access token?
expectations: Covers both approaches: Info.plist (MBXAccessToken key) for Xcode-managed projects, and Config.swift + MapboxOptions.accessToken for SPM/xcodegen projects
For the Config.swift approach: sets MapboxOptions.accessToken in the App init(), keeps Config.swift gitignored, commits Config.swift.example as a template
For the Info.plist approach: shows <key>MBXAccessToken</key> <string>pk.your_token</string> and notes the SDK reads it automatically
Notes the token should be a public token (starts with pk.)

evals.prompt: My iOS app creates a new `PointAnnotationManager` inside `updateMarkers()` every time markers change, and performance is bad when called frequently. What's wrong?
expectations: Creating a new annotation manager on every update is the problem — managers should be created once and reused
Store the PointAnnotationManager as an instance property and initialize it once
To update markers, just reassign the annotations array: pointAnnotationManager.annotations = newAnnotations
Also recommends batch updates: set all annotations at once rather than appending one by one

evals.prompt: I'm using the Mapbox Standard style on iOS and want to detect when users tap on POIs (coffee shops, restaurants, etc.) on the map. How do I implement this?
expectations: Use the Interactions API with TapInteraction(.standardPoi) — the modern recommended approach for Standard style featuresets
Shows the SwiftUI or UIKit pattern: TapInteraction(.standardPoi) { poi, context in ... }
The poi object provides typed access to POI properties like poi.name
Notes that returning true from the closure stops propagation to other interactions

evals.prompt: I want to build an iOS app with Mapbox Maps SDK using Swift Package Manager. I created a Package.swift with a .target, added the MapboxMaps dependency, but when I hit Run in Xcode nothing launches. What am I missing?
expectations: A bare SPM .target builds as a library, not an .app bundle — it cannot be launched as an iOS app
Recommends creating a proper Xcode project using xcodegen with a project.yml, or using File > New > Project in Xcode
With xcodegen: brew install xcodegen, write project.yml with type: application, run xcodegen generate, open the .xcodeproj
The generated .xcodeproj should be gitignored; project.yml is committed as the source of truth

evals.prompt: I'm building a SwiftUI iOS app with Mapbox. I have a list of coffee shops and want to show circle markers on the map. When a user taps a circle, I want to show a callout label above it. How do I do this in SwiftUI without UIViewRepresentable?
expectations: Uses CircleAnnotationGroup(shops) with a closure producing CircleAnnotation per shop — not UIViewRepresentable
Each CircleAnnotation has .onTapGesture { selectedShop = shop } to handle taps
Uses MapViewAnnotation(coordinate: selected.coordinate) with a SwiftUI view inside for the callout label
MapViewAnnotation uses .allowOverlap(true) and .variableAnchors([ViewAnnotationAnchorConfig(anchor: .bottom)]) to position above the marker
Does NOT use UIViewRepresentable or Coordinator classes

evals.prompt: In my SwiftUI Mapbox app, when a user selects a location from a list I want the map to fly to that location with an animated transition. How do I animate the camera in SwiftUI?
expectations: Uses withViewportAnimation(.fly(duration: 0.8)) wrapping a viewport state update
Sets viewport = .camera(center: coordinate, zoom: 16) inside the withViewportAnimation block
Does NOT use UIKit mapView.camera.fly(to:) — that's UIKit only
Triggered via .onChange(of: selectedItem) or a tap handler

evals.prompt: I'm trying to set a circle color in my SwiftUI Mapbox app using StyleColor(red: 0.44, green: 0.31, blue: 0.22, alpha: 1) but the compiler says the value is optional. How do I fix this?
expectations: StyleColor(red:green:blue:alpha:) returns StyleColor? (optional) — this initializer can fail
The fix is to use StyleColor(UIColor(red: 0.44, green: 0.31, blue: 0.22, alpha: 1)) which returns a non-optional StyleColor
Alternatively use StyleColor(.systemBrown) or any UIColor-based initializer
